request: We should know which of our contacts are most influential so we can prioritize them.
pre_mortem: A year after launch, the influence scoring feature resulted in a serious incident where a regional coordinator mistakenly assigned high influence scores to contacts who had minimal engagement with the organization. As a result, project managers prioritized meetings with these contacts, leading to wasted resources and missed opportunities with more strategically important stakeholders. The misallocation of time and effort created frustration within teams and damaged relationships with key partners.
gaps: What guidelines exist to ensure consistent understanding of 'influence' among users?
What permissions restrict who can view or edit influence scores to protect sensitive data?

Who is responsible for auditing the influence scores and ensuring they align with actual engagement and influence?
What happens when a user leaves or changes roles; how are their influence score assignments managed?
How will this feature address potential bias in assigning influence scores among users?

proposals.summary: This release will implement a feature that allows users to categorize and identify influential contacts within the Government CRM. It will provide regional coordinators, project managers, and executive-level staff with the ability to prioritize engagements based on influence levels of contacts.

core_commitments.text: Users will be able to assign an influence score to each contact within the Government CRM.
Users will see a prioritized list of contacts based on their influence scores.

in_scope.text: Regional coordinators, project managers, and executive-level staff will be able to assign influence scores to contacts on a scale of 1-5, where 1 means low influence and 5 means high influence.
The contact list will display the assigned influence scores alongside contact names to help users quickly identify influential contacts.
Users will have the ability to filter the contact list based on influence scores to prioritize engagements.
The feature will include permissions so only users with appropriate roles can assign influence scores.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not include any automated or algorithm-driven scoring system for influence; the scores will be manually assigned by users.
This release will not change existing contact record fields outside the influence scoring.

assumptions.text: Users are familiar with the concept of influence scoring and understand how to use a scoring system; this knowledge is required for effective use of the feature.
Contact information is accurate and up-to-date in the system, allowing for meaningful influence assessments.
There is a clear understanding of what constitutes 'influence' among users; this understanding is needed to create consistent scoring.

definitions.text: "influence score" means a numerical value assigned to a contact that represents their level of influence, rated on a scale of 1 (low influence) to 5 (high influence).
"prioritized list" means an ordered list of contacts displayed in the Government CRM that reflects their influence scores, with the highest scores appearing first.

success_criteria.text: At least 75% of users assign influence scores to their contacts within the first month of release, measured by system usage analytics.
Users report a satisfaction rating of 80% or higher in a post-release survey regarding the usefulness of the influence feature for contact prioritization.

C1.challenge: The term 'influence' is not adequately defined or standardized, leading to inconsistent application among users, which could result in significant errors in engagement prioritization.

C1.resolution_test: What specific criteria will be established to define 'influence' for consistent scoring across all users?
